verification_report.summary: The entire supplied reconstruction is correct under the declared internal and standard premises. All 15 sequential proof checks and all reference checks pass. The sign dc d = -d dc makes j_X well defined and gives the stated kernel of real parts of closed holomorphic one-forms. Full distributional Gauduchon traces, including unbounded genuine qpsh potentials, establish lineality and distinguish nonzero positive currents from the zero Bott–Chern class. Elliptic regularity justifies passage back to smooth Bott–Chern cohomology. The annihilator argument proves image(q_X)=W_X, and positive roots and finite-dimensional perturbations prove nonemptiness, convexity, span and openness in W_X. Lamari and finite-dimensional separation yield both dual formulas, with strict tests precisely outside K_X and with W_X=0 handled correctly. Modification pullback is constructed from local psh potentials; distributional pushforward and elliptic smoothing establish pseudoeffectivity in both directions and Bott–Chern injectivity. Thom theory proves the H^1 blowup isomorphism, whose Poincare dual correctly maps H^(2n-1)(Y) to H^(2n-1)(X). General position proves independence of factorization. The required compact complex factorization, including preservation of the common open set, is explicitly supplied by [AKMW Theorem 0.3.1(2)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9904135v4). The balanced equivalences, Fujiki conclusion and Hopf half-line computation follow. The proof neither identifies image(j_X) with every de Rham-exact Bott–Chern class nor infers pseudoeffectivity from one positive test. It assumes neither LCK geometry nor bounded Monge–Ampere mass for the cone results, and makes no assertion that ordinary perturbations remain LCK or Vaisman. [OV Theorems 3.11 and 4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.05595v2) match the attribution; the reconstruction independently establishes its pairing sign and kernel qualification rather than importing the printed strict formula. Detailed deductions and source comparisons are persisted in this run's memory.
